source_of_truth: The frozen judge-only reference dossier; candidates answer from internal knowledge.
evaluation_principles: Require physical balancing rather than annual-energy arithmetic.
Reward matching flexibility resources to timescales.
Preserve the real but limited value of annual procurement.

key_facts.label: Annual totals are not hourly supply
key_facts.expected: Explains that equal annual consumption and renewable procurement do not establish simultaneous physical supply.

key_facts.label: Continuous balancing and residual load
key_facts.expected: Defines the need to balance demand against variable output and explains residual or net load.

key_facts.label: Curtailment
key_facts.expected: Explains surplus curtailment and why it can be rational yet reveal missing flexibility or grids.

key_facts.label: Storage constraints
key_facts.expected: Distinguishes power, energy, duration and losses and rejects a generic battery solution for all timescales.

key_facts.label: Grid and geographic diversity
key_facts.expected: Explains the value and limits of transmission and interconnection.

key_facts.label: Demand flexibility
key_facts.expected: Explains load shifting or reduction and its practical limits.

key_facts.label: Other long-duration flexibility
key_facts.expected: Includes longer-duration storage or dispatchable low-emissions supply for longer scarcity periods.

key_facts.label: Hourly matching trade-offs
key_facts.expected: Covers better temporal alignment plus cost, overbuilding, location and additionality caveats.

key_ideas.label: Energy quantity versus availability
key_ideas.expected: Separates annual energy accounting from when and where power is available.

key_ideas.label: Portfolio across timescales
key_ideas.expected: Matches diverse flexibility resources to short, multi-day and seasonal needs.

key_ideas.label: Accounting versus causal impact
key_ideas.expected: Separates contractual attribution from additional generation and actual system emissions changes.

key_ideas.label: System-dependent optimization
key_ideas.expected: Rejects universal technology recipes and recognizes system context and coordination.

known_critical_errors.description: Claims that 100% annual matching proves 24/7 physical renewable supply.
Claims that any unspecified battery can cover all balancing and seasonal needs.
Claims annual renewable procurement has no possible emissions or investment value.
Conflates grid reliability with zero emissions.
Claims transmission or geographic diversity eliminates all prolonged correlated scarcity.

anchors.25: No material power-system or emissions-accounting error.
anchors.20: Accurate overall with one minor imprecision.
anchors.12: At least one major error or several meaningful imprecisions.

anchors.10: Connects temporal mismatch, residual load and a multi-timescale flexibility portfolio.
anchors.7: Sound explanation with one underdeveloped connection.
anchors.4: Lists technologies without explaining the system problem.

anchors.10: Calibrates benefits and limits without categorical technology claims.
anchors.7: Mostly calibrated with one limited overstatement.
anchors.4: Repeatedly presents contingent outcomes as automatic.

anchors.10: Clear German, descriptive structure and understandable without power-system training.

anchors.5: High information density without material repetition.
anchors.0: Exceeds the hard maximum or is not focused.
